**Visual analysis:**

- Two sugarcane leaves side by side
- Predominantly green leaf blades with a prominent white/pale stripe running along the midrib
- Numerous small, scattered tan-to-brownish spots distributed across the green leaf surface
- Leaf shape and texture otherwise appear normal (no twisting, no mosaic patterning, no longitudinal streaks)

**Ruling out other classes:**

- **Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus / Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv**: No mosaic or longitudinal interveinal streak patterns — just discrete spots
- **Leaf_Scald**: White pencil line goes from midrib to margin (transverse); no scalded/burned necrosis
- **Yellow_Leaf**: Would show midrib yellowing progressing to necrosis, not discrete spots
- **Grassy_Shoot / Pokkah_Boeng**: No bushy tillering, no twisting/wrinkling, no knife-cut damage
- **Sett_Rot**: Affects stem/sett, not leaf surface spots
- **Yellow_Spot**: Spots would be more clearly yellow/elongated

**Key match — Brown_Spot**: The numerous small, round, scattered tan-brown spots on a green sugarcane leaf are the hallmark of Brown Spot disease (*Bipolaris sacchari*), which produces exactly this pattern of discrete lesions distributed across the leaf blade. The pale midrib is consistent with central vein involvement seen in advanced cases.
